subject: The QMCEM iteration problem with itemfit statistics over 3 factors

messages.author: 6a75f6f91a59c568
messages.subject: The QMCEM iteration problem with itemfit statistics over 3 factors
parts:
Hello Phil,

I'm trying calculate item fit statistics with a model having over 3 factors.

So, I executed these codes;

  message('estimating Theta')
  try(test2_fscores <- fscores(object = result, rotate = 'geominQ', full.scores = T, plausible.draws = 100, QMC = TRUE, method = 'MAP', MI = 100))
  message('estimating itemfit')
  try(test2 <- itemfit(result, method = 'MAP', Theta = test2_fscores, impute = 100, QMC = TRUE, Zh = F), silent = T)
  
But, itemfit() returns these warnings;

Warning message: High-Dimensional models should use quasi-Monte Carlo integration PASS QMC=TRUE
Warning message: High-Dimensional models should use quasi-Monte Carlo integration PASS QMC=TRUE
EM quadrature for high dimensional models are better handled with the "QMCEM" method
EM quadrature for high dimensional models are better handled with the "QMCEM" method
EM quadrature for high dimensional models are better handled with the "QMCEM" method
EM quadrature for high dimensional models are better handled with the "QMCEM" method
EM quadrature for high dimensional models are better handled with the "QMCEM" method

Was my syntax wrong?

I'm using 1.13 on CRAN. Cheers.

--
Best regards,
Seongho Bae

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: The QMCEM iteration problem with itemfit statistics over 3 factors
parts:
Hi Seongho,

Nothing was wrong with your syntax, but the method = 'MAP' argument was being ignored when generating plausible values and was defaulting to EAP instead. Just patched this on the dev version, so your syntax shouldn't throw any more warnings. Cheers.

Phil
